notes: The fix is correct and complete, with inline checks and doc-comment updates matching the reference. Tests are extensive, but it rewrites an existing snippet test's inputs and expectations rather than adding a separate case, which muddies that test's original intent.

The fix matches the reference with inline `Quoted()` checks and updated doc comments, and the tests are very thorough (including `{}` and standalone tokens). It edits an existing snippet test instead of adding a new one, and the repeated inline conditions are a bit verbose.

Inline `Quoted()` checks cover every brace check the reference touches, including the import `switch` and the `{}` handling. Tests cover all three quote styles across many parse contexts, plus an imported-snippet case and an integration adapt test; the repeated inline conditions are slightly verbose.

Makes the same changes as the reference with inline checks. Tests are extensive across quote styles and brace forms, with dedicated NextArg and NextBlock tests, an imported-snippet `{block}` regression test, and an integration fixture.

Code is functionally identical to C1, with every structural brace check made quote-aware. Tests are comprehensive: dispenser args/block/nesting, many parse contexts including an imported block placeholder and named routes, plus an integration adapt test.

Makes the same changes as the reference using inline `Quoted()` checks. Tests include dispenser cases, many parse contexts (including an imported snippet with `{block}`, named routes and checks on keys and route flags) and an adapt integration fixture.

Adds a small `Token.isUnquoted` helper, close to the reference's approach, and applies it consistently across the dispenser and parser. Tests are thorough and include dispenser nesting checks, parse contexts, an imported snippet definition and adapter-level `respond` tests.

Changes every brace check the reference changes and uses a small `Token.isUnquoted` helper, which is idiomatic. Tests cover dispenser behavior, the parse contexts, imported snippets and the adapter across all three quote styles; the only gap is that the RemainingArgs doc comments were not updated.

Concise per-resource slice fix with good tests (refactoring unit test plus plan tests covering for_each/count, reversed order and modules), but parent blocks still suppress child blocks for different instances, unlike the reference's instance-level dedup.

Fixes the root-module for_each/count drop by grouping imports per ConfigResource and keeping same-module duplicates, but a parent block still overrides at the config-resource level rather than per instance, so a child module's imports of other instances are silently discarded. That is the same class of bug, and it accounts for the 2/3 hidden tests failing; tests are strong (unit test plus for_each/count, order-reversal and in-module plan tests).

Fixes the reported root-module case by keeping every same-module block per ConfigResource; still drops a child module's block when a parent block targets a different instance of the same resource, and the TargetContains loop is more convoluted than needed.

Uses a map of slices with a somewhat convoluted ancestor check (the TargetContains check is redundant given the traversal order), and fixes same-module multi-instance imports. It still drops a child module's imports of different instances whenever a parent targets the same resource; only a single basic test is added.

The new ordered-list discovery with an inherited set is clean and fixes the reported case, but parent/child override is still decided per ConfigResource rather than per instance, and the old first-wins FindImportStatements is kept as dead code.

Essentially the same design as C2: a new FindAllImportStatements with an inherited set, while the old dedup-by-ConfigResource function is kept but unused. It fixes the issue's scenario but not instance-level parent/child override, and adds one basic for_each test.

Essentially the same as C2: a list-based discovery that fixes the reported case, but it keeps the legacy map function that explicitly preserves the buggy first-entry behavior, and it misses instance-level parent/child override.

Adds FindImportStatementsList with a clean ancestor-claimed set, which fixes the reported case, but it keeps parent-overrides-child at config-resource rather than instance granularity.
